title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 7, WITH NEPHROPATHY AND DEAFNESS
alt_titles: NEPHROPATHY WITH PRETIBIAL EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA AND DEAFNESS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene (602243) on chromosome 11p15.5.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3 patients are homozygous for a single nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151, causing a frameshift and premature stop signal at codon 140.
checks.explanation: Patients with nephritis, deafness and pretibial EB are homozygous for a CD151 mutation; the disease name EBS7 is not used in the paper but the phenotype corresponds.

checks.claim: The CD151 gene is located on chromosome 11p15.5.
checks.evidence_quote: It is encoded by a gene at the same position on chromosome 11p15.5 as the MER2 blood group gene.

paragraphs.text: EBS7 is an autosomal recessive disorder characterized by hereditary nephritis progressing to end-stage kidney disease, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and sensorineural deafness. Affected individuals are negative for the MER2 blood group antigen, which is carried by CD151 (Karamatic Crew et al., 2004).

checks.claim: EBS7 is an autosomal recessive disorder.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3 patients are homozygous for a single nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151
checks.explanation: The abstract does not state an inheritance pattern. Homozygosity in affected patients, including 2 siblings, is consistent with autosomal recessive inheritance.

paragraphs.text: In 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, including 2 sibs who also had sensorineural deafness, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and beta-thalassemia minor, Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) identified homozygosity for a 1-bp insertion (G383) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene, causing a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140. The resulting truncated protein would lack its integrin-binding domain.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) noted that CD151 forms very stable laminin-binding complexes with integrins alpha-3/beta-1 and alpha-6/beta-1 in kidney and alpha-3/beta-1 and alpha-6/beta-4 in skin. From their findings in patients with a truncating CD151 mutation, they concluded that CD151 is essential for the proper assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membrane in kidney and has functional significance in skin, is probably a component of the inner ear, and could play a role in erythropoiesis.
